benchmark_details.name: BGPT REFUTE
benchmark_details.overview: A text-only benchmark for evaluating whether language models can critique recent scientific paper summaries with evidence-grounded judgment and calibrated uncertainty rather than persuasive overconfidence.
benchmark_details.data_type: Text generation, scientific critique, calibration vignettes

purpose_and_intended_users.goal: To evaluate scientific judgment in language models by separating critique skill from epistemic truthfulness, calibration, and flaw discrimination.
purpose_and_intended_users.limitations: Rubric-scored critique tasks use LLM judges; the benchmark is text-only, science-heavy, and small relative to broad multitask suites; soundness vignettes come from a single authoring pipeline; length control mitigates but does not eliminate residual length correlation.
out_of_scope_uses: General-purpose model capability ranking without axis-level interpretation
Clinical or policy decision-making without human expert review
Treating composite Truth Score as a substitute for reviewing calibration, skill, and discrimination separately

data.source: Structured summaries of recent 2025-2026 science papers, plus objective sound/flawed vignettes for calibration and flaw-detection axes.
data.size: 120 full benchmark items, 60-item challenge subset, and 74 soundness/calibration vignettes.
data.format: Hugging Face dataset with three configurations: refute_120, refute_hard_60, and refute_soundness.
data.annotation: Items include paper cards, reference answer sketches, task-specific rubrics, scoring notes, and objective sound/flawed labels for the soundness split.

methods: Rubric-based LLM judge panel for critique skill
Cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals and statistical tiers
metrics: Composite Truth Score for complete-axis runs
methodology.calculation: Model answers are scored on independent evidence channels. Critique answers are judged with strict rubrics; calibration uses Brier loss on probability estimates; forced-choice tasks use accuracy and confidence intervals; the optional Truth Score combines complete axes.
methodology.interpretation: Users should interpret REFUTE by axis. High critique skill does not imply calibrated truthfulness, and within-tier model differences should not be overinterpreted.
methodology.baseline_results: A June 2026 panel evaluated 19 frontier models. Grok-family models formed the top critique-skill tier, while GLM-5.1 narrowly led composite Truth Score through stronger calibration.
methodology.validation: The release reports length-control analysis, judge negative controls, judge-free forced-choice and soundness axes, confidence intervals, and benchmark limitations.

subcategory: Model behavior instability under evidence gaps

targeted_risks.demographic_analysis: Not applicable; the benchmark focuses on scientific reasoning and evidence assessment rather than demographic groups.
targeted_risks.harm: Misusing fluent model critiques as authoritative scientific review could lead to unsupported conclusions, false confidence, or poor research decisions.

ethical_and_legal_considerations.privacy_and_anonymity: The public release is based on structured scientific paper summaries and benchmark prompts, not private personal data.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.compliance_with_regulations: Users remain responsible for applying the benchmark in accordance with research, publication, and domain-specific governance requirements.
